Due to Solidity's integer division rounding down, an attacker can cause legitimate deposits to result in 0 shares, while the deposited tokens remain in the vault. <|det|>text [81, 234, 874, 249]<|/det|>The shares calculation in AlgebraVault.deposit() uses integer division that rounds down: <|det|>text [102, 284, 805, 405]<|/det|>if (_totalSupply != 0) { uint256 priceForPool = _getConservativePrice(price, twap, auxTwap, true); uint256 poolOfPricedInToken1 = pool0.mul(priceForPool).div(PRECISION); shares = shares.mul(_totalSupply).div(poolOfPricedInToken1.add(pool1)); } else { shares = shares.mul(MIN_SHARES); } <|det|>text [80, 438, 895, 504]<|/det|>If shares rounds down to 0, the function mints 0 shares to the user, but the deposited tokens remain in the vault. When the attacker withdraws their shares, they receive a proportional share of ALL tokens in the vault, including the tokens deposited by users who received 0 shares. <|det|>title [81, 508, 232, 520]<|/det|>Attack Scenario: <|det|>text [83, 524, 848, 539]<|/det|>1. Attacker deposits 1 wei and receives 1000 shares (MIN_SHARES), totalSupply = 1000 <|det|>text [83, 542, 603, 556]<|/det|>2. Attacker transfers 1000e6 tokens directly to the vault <|det|>text [83, 560, 538, 574]<|/det|>3. Legitimate user attempts to deposit 1e6 tokens: <|det|>text [110, 576, 667, 625]<|/det|>- shares = 1e6 * 1000 / (1000e6 + 1) = 0 (rounds down to 0) - _mint(user, 0) is called, but 1e6 tokens remain in the vault - Vault balance: 1000e6 + 1 + 1e6 = 1001000001 wei <|det|>text [82, 635, 871, 666]<|/det|>4. Attacker withdraws all 1000 shares and receives ALL tokens, including the user's 1e6 deposit: <|det|>text [102, 704, 777, 877]<|/det|>uint256 unusedAmount0 = IERC20(token0) .balanceOf(address(this)) .mul(shares) .div(_totalSupply); uint256 unusedAmount1 = IERC20(token1) .balanceOf(address(this)) .mul(shares) .div(_totalSupply); if (unusedAmount0 > 0) IERC20(token0).safeTransfer(to, unusedAmount0); if (unusedAmount1 > 0) IERC20(token1).safeTransfer(to, unusedAmount1); <|det|>text [80, 907, 895, 940]<|/det|>This issue is classified Low severity because while it theoretically allows an attacker to steal user deposits, in practice most users will interact with the vault through <|det|>footer [81, 949, 248, 972]<|/det|>MixBytes() <|det|>page_number [880, 951, 916, 970]<|/det|>22

<PAGE><|det|>text [80, 58, 915, 125]<|/det|>AlgebraVaultDepositGuard, which includes a slippage check. If a user receives 0 shares, the transaction will revert when minimumProceeds > 0, which is the expected behavior. The attack is only viable if users deposit directly to the vault (bypassing AlgebraVaultDepositGuard) or set minimumProceeds = 0 in the guard, both of which are unlikely scenarios.
<|det|>title [81, 145, 212, 158]<|/det|>Recommendation
<|det|>text [80, 162, 899, 248]<|/det|>We recommend increasing the MIN_SHARES constant from 1000 to 1e6 and adding a check to prevent minting 0 shares. Increasing MIN_SHARES to 1e6 significantly increases the cost of the attack – with MIN_SHARES = 1e6, if the first deposit is 1 wei for 1e6 shares, an attacker would need to donate more than 1e12 tokens to cause a 1e6 token deposit to result in 0 shares, making the attack economically unfeasible.
<|det|>text [102, 281, 805, 436]<|/det|>if (_totalSupply != 0) {
    uint256 priceForPool = _getConservativePrice(price, twap, auxTwap, true);
    uint256 poolOpRedInToken1 = pool0.mul(priceForPool).div(PRECISION);
    shares = shares.mul(_totalSupply).div(pool0pRedInToken1.add(pool1));

    ++ if (shares == 0) revert InvalidDeposit();
} else {
    shares = shares.mul(MIN_SHARES);
}
